correctness.rationale: The packaged executable exhaustively builds one color of each even board size 2,4,6, verifies all faces via independent subset methods, tests all Hasse orientations for acyclicity, and carries out exact signed augmented-chain cancellation with unit pivots; remaining integer Morse boundary matrices are identically zero. On board 6, 409 faces, 1206 incidences, 196 pairs and 14 two- plus 3 three-dimensional critical cells are verified. Hurewicz gives nullhomotopic 3-cell attaching maps in the simply connected wedge of 14 two-spheres. The opposite-color factor is isomorphic by reflection, and the simplicial join/suspension-smash identity rigorously yields 196,84,9 sphere summands at dimensions 5,6,7. Boards 2 and 4 are likewise completely checked and prove the exact first-even threshold.

originality.rationale: The full arXiv primary text of Clark--Zeckner was materially compared: its triangular Ferrers shapes include rows of every positive length, while the bishop-color six-board Ferrers partition is (6,4,4,2,2). Its vertex-decomposability and Stirling-complex results do not contain these wedge ranks. Harris et al. address cardinality extrema for bishop positions, not these attaching maps. Closely related published index records about matching complexes of Cartesian/categorical grid graphs concern nonisomorphic complexes. The distinct five-board problem cannot imply this six-board homotopy or the first even size. Searches by aliases, exact parameters, and stronger homotopy coverage found no implication; residual unindexed-source risk persists.

value.rationale: The nonattacking-bishop placement complex is a natural flag simplicial complex attached to an established board-packing problem. For the smallest three even square boards it exhibits a substantive change from single-degree integral homotopy to three different sphere dimensions. An exact canonical first-cutoff classification is relevant for Ferrers-board matching-complex homotopy and cannot be deduced from rook/bishop counts, independence numbers, or the prior odd five-board computation. The result does not rely on a claimed infinite family.
